TOPIC_COLUMNS = ["pro_just_transition", "anti_ff", "pro_ff", "energy_security"]
TOPIC_LABELS = {
    "pro_just_transition": "pro\\_just\\_transition",
    "anti_ff": "anti\\_ff",
    "pro_ff": "pro\\_ff",
    "energy_security": "energy\\_security",
}

PARTY_SHORT_NAMES = {
    2022: {
        "Fajardo (Centro Esperanza)": "Fajardo",
        "Gutiérrez (Equipo por Colombia)": "Gutiérrez",
        "Hernández (Liga Anticorrupción)": "Hernández",
        "Petro (Pacto Histórico)": "Pacto Histórico",
    },
    2026: {
        "De la Espriella": "De la Espriella",
        "Dignidad y Compromiso": "Dignidad y Compromiso",
        "Pacto Histórico (Petro's party)": "Pacto Histórico",
        "Plan Integrado de Gobierno": "Plan Integrado de Gobierno",
    },
}


def topic_percentage_panel(year):
    year_df = corrected_df[corrected_df["year"] == year]
    short_names = PARTY_SHORT_NAMES[year]
    parties = sorted(short_names, key=lambda full_name: short_names[full_name])

    column_spec = "p{0.15\\textwidth} | C{0.12\\textwidth} | " + " | ".join(
        "C{0.10\\textwidth}" for _ in parties
    )
    header = " & ".join([r"\textbf{Topic}", r"\textbf{All Manifestos}"] + [
        f"\\textbf{{{short_names[party]}}}" for party in parties
    ])

    lines = [
        f"  \\textbf{{{year}}}\\\\[2pt]",
        f"  \\begin{{tabular}}{{{column_spec}}}",
        "  \\toprule",
        f"  {header} \\\\",
        "  \\midrule",
    ]

    # Calculate topic percentages
    for topic in TOPIC_COLUMNS:
        all_pct = (year_df["year"] == year).sum()
        if all_pct > 0:
            # Count sentences with this topic flagged
            topic_count = (year_df[topic] == 1).sum()
            all_pct_val = (topic_count / len(year_df)) * 100
        else:
            all_pct_val = 0

        party_pcts = []
        for party in parties:
            party_df = year_df[year_df["manifesto"] == party]
            if len(party_df) > 0:
                party_topic_count = (party_df[topic] == 1).sum()
                party_pct_val = (party_topic_count / len(party_df)) * 100
            else:
                party_pct_val = 0
            party_pcts.append(f"{party_pct_val:.1f}\\,\\%")

        topic_label = TOPIC_LABELS[topic]
        party_str = " & ".join(party_pcts)
        lines.append(f"  {topic_label} & {all_pct_val:.1f}\\,\\% & {party_str} \\\\")

    lines.append("  \\bottomrule")
    lines.append("  \\end{tabular}")
    return "\n".join(lines)


table_lines = [
    r"\begin{table}[htbp]",
    r"  \centering",
    r"  \tiny",
    r"  \caption{Topic percentages in all manifestos and specific parties, 2022 and 2026}",
    topic_percentage_panel(2022),
    r"  \vspace{6pt}",
    topic_percentage_panel(2026),
    r"  \label{tab:topic_percentages_by_party_year}",
    r"\end{table}",
]

latex_output = "\n".join(table_lines)
print(latex_output)

# Manifesto-level LaTeX table: policlim climate salience and LLM-derived topic shares
# (all as a percentage of each manifesto's total sentence count), by year. Uses the
# comparison table saved above, so it can be run standalone without re-running the
# extraction/classification pipeline. Printed only - nothing is written to disk here.
policlim_vs_llm_path = COMPARISON_DIR / "policlim_vs_llm_manifesto_scores.csv"
policlim_vs_llm_table = pd.read_csv(policlim_vs_llm_path)

# (year, label as it appears in policlim_vs_llm_table) -> the display text this table
# uses for the Manifesto column. The 2026 rows show the actual 2026 candidate surname
# and party (per MANIFESTO_TO_CANDIDATE_2026 above), not the manifesto_id label, since
# the label still names the 2022 candidate/programme the PDF was filed under.
MANIFESTO_ROW_ORDER = [
    (2022, "Hernández (Liga Anticorrupción)", "Hernández", "Liga Anticorrupción", False),
    (2022, "Petro (Pacto Histórico)", "Petro", "Pacto Histórico", True),
    (2022, "Gutiérrez (Equipo por Colombia)", "Gutiérrez", "Equipo por Colombia", False),
    (2022, "Fajardo (Centro Esperanza)", "Fajardo", "Centro Esperanza", False),
    (2026, "De la Espriella", "De la Espriella", "Defensores de la Patria", True),
    (2026, "Pacto Histórico (Petro's party)", "Cepeda", "Pacto Histórico", False),
    (2026, "Plan Integrado de Gobierno", "Valencia", "Centro Democrático", False),
    (2026, "Dignidad y Compromiso", "Fajardo", "Dignidad y Compromiso", False),
]

SCORE_COLUMNS = ["climate_salience_share", "Pro-just transition", "Anti fossil fuel", "Pro fossil fuel", "Energy security"]

rows_latex = []
column_values = {col: [] for col in SCORE_COLUMNS}
for year, label, surname, party, is_starred in MANIFESTO_ROW_ORDER:
    match = policlim_vs_llm_table[
        (policlim_vs_llm_table["year"] == year) & (policlim_vs_llm_table["label"] == label)
    ]
    data_row = match.iloc[0]
    star = "*" if is_starred else ""
    party_cell = f"{party}{star}"
    values = " & ".join(f"{data_row[col] * 100:.1f}" for col in SCORE_COLUMNS)
    rows_latex.append(f"    {year} & {party_cell} & {surname} & {values} \\\\")
    for col in SCORE_COLUMNS:
        column_values[col].append(data_row[col] * 100)

# Unweighted average across the 8 manifesto-year rows above (not weighted by sentence count).
average_values = " & ".join(
    f"\\textbf{{{sum(column_values[col]) / len(column_values[col]):.1f}}}" for col in SCORE_COLUMNS
)
rows_latex.append("    \\midrule")
rows_latex.append(f"     &  & \\textbf{{Average}} & {average_values} \\\\")

latex_table = (
    r"\begin{table}[htbp]" + "\n"
    r"  \centering" + "\n"
    r"  \small" + "\n"
    r"  \caption{Climate salience and LLM topic shares by manifesto, 2022 and 2026}" + "\n"
    r"  \begin{tabular}{|r|l|c|r|r|r|r|r|}" + "\n"
    r"  \toprule" + "\n"
    r"  \textbf{Year} & \textbf{Party} & \textbf{Candidate} & \textbf{Climate Salience} & \textbf{Just Transition} & \textbf{Anti-FF} & \textbf{Pro-FF} & \textbf{Energy Sec.} \\" + "\n"
    r"  \midrule" + "\n"
    + "\n".join(rows_latex) + "\n"
    r"  \end{tabular}%" + "\n"
    r"  \label{tab:municipio_manifesto_summary_llm}%" + "\n"
    r"\end{table}%" + "\n"
)

# Export the final manifesto-level results at candidate x year level to one Excel workbook
# with two sheets, both excluding Claudia López:
#   - "scores":         the five manifesto scores as shares of all sentences in the manifesto
#                       (policlim climate salience + the four LLM categories), recomputed here
#                       from corrected_df - the LLM classifications after the manual validation
#                       corrections above - rather than read from policlim_vs_llm_manifesto_scores.csv,
#                       which was built from the uncorrected LLM output.
#                       The mining-stance dummies (pro_mining / reformist / contra_mining) are
#                       included in this sheet as well, so it holds every candidate-year variable.
#   - "party_families": each manifesto's mining stance (pro_mining / reformist / contra_mining)
#                       as 1/0 dummies only.
# The stance is hard-coded below from the "Stance" column of the counts_with_stance table
# (majority category, ties -> Reformist), so this cell does not depend on the reformist
# classification cells having run; update MANIFESTO_STANCE if that table changes.
# Candidate names follow the electoral data (Title Case DES_CAN), so both sheets merge directly
# onto data/electoral/processed/candidate_merged_voting_data.xlsx on (year, candidate).
# Fajardo is "Sergio Fajardo" in both years.
EXCLUDED_MANIFESTOS = {"Claudia López"}

# (year, manifesto label) -> assigned mining stance, per the stance table above
MANIFESTO_STANCE = {
    (2022, "Fajardo (Centro Esperanza)"):      "Contra-mining",
    (2022, "Gutiérrez (Equipo por Colombia)"): "Pro-mining",
    (2022, "Hernández (Liga Anticorrupción)"): "Reformist",
    (2022, "Petro (Pacto Histórico)"):         "Contra-mining",
    (2026, "De la Espriella"):                 "Pro-mining",
    (2026, "Dignidad y Compromiso"):           "Reformist",
    (2026, "Pacto Histórico (Petro's party)"): "Reformist",
    (2026, "Plan Integrado de Gobierno"):      "Pro-mining",
}
FAMILY_COLUMNS = {"pro_mining": "Pro-mining", "reformist": "Reformist", "contra_mining": "Contra-mining"}

# (year, manifesto label as used in summary_df / corrected_df / reformist_df) -> (candidate, party)
LABEL_TO_CANDIDATE = {
    (2022, "Fajardo (Centro Esperanza)"):      ("Sergio Fajardo",           "Centro Esperanza"),
    (2022, "Gutiérrez (Equipo por Colombia)"): ("Federico Gutiérrez",       "Equipo por Colombia"),
    (2022, "Hernández (Liga Anticorrupción)"): ("Rodolfo Hernández",        "Liga Anticorrupción"),
    (2022, "Petro (Pacto Histórico)"):         ("Gustavo Petro",            "Pacto Histórico"),
    (2026, "De la Espriella"):                 ("Abelardo De La Espriella", "Defensores de la Patria"),
    (2026, "Pacto Histórico (Petro's party)"): ("Iván Cepeda Castro",       "Pacto Histórico"),
    (2026, "Plan Integrado de Gobierno"):      ("Paloma Valencia Laserna",  "Centro Democrático"),
    (2026, "Dignidad y Compromiso"):           ("Sergio Fajardo",           "Dignidad y Compromiso"),
}


def to_candidate_level(frame, year_col, label_col, value_cols):
    """Drop excluded manifestos, attach candidate/party, keep value_cols, one row per candidate-year."""
    frame = frame[~frame[label_col].isin(EXCLUDED_MANIFESTOS)]
    keys = list(zip(frame[year_col].astype(int), frame[label_col]))
    unmapped = sorted({key for key in keys if key not in LABEL_TO_CANDIDATE})
    if unmapped:
        raise KeyError(f"No candidate mapping for manifesto(s): {unmapped}")
    out = pd.DataFrame({
        "year": [key[0] for key in keys],
        "candidate": [LABEL_TO_CANDIDATE[key][0] for key in keys],
        "party": [LABEL_TO_CANDIDATE[key][1] for key in keys],
        "manifesto_label": [key[1] for key in keys],
    })
    for col in value_cols:
        out[col] = frame[col].to_numpy()
    return out.sort_values(["year", "candidate"]).reset_index(drop=True)


def add_family_dummies(frame):
    """Attach the hard-coded stance as 1/0 columns (exactly one of them 1) plus its label."""
    stances = [MANIFESTO_STANCE[(year, label)] for year, label in zip(frame["year"], frame["manifesto_label"])]
    for column, stance_label in FAMILY_COLUMNS.items():
        frame[column] = [int(stance == stance_label) for stance in stances]
    frame["stance"] = stances
    assert (frame[list(FAMILY_COLUMNS)].sum(axis=1) == 1).all(), "each candidate-year must have exactly one stance"
    return frame


# --- Sheet 1: scores, from the validated classifications ---------------------------------
if "summary_df" not in globals():
    summary_df = pd.read_csv(COMPARISON_DIR / "policlim_manifesto_summary_all_years.csv")

LLM_CATEGORIES = ["pro_just_transition", "anti_ff", "pro_ff", "energy_security"]

# Same construction as policlim_vs_llm above: corrected_df only holds the high-score (>=0.8)
# subset, so count flagged sentences per manifesto and divide by the manifesto's full
# sentence_count to get the share of all sentences in the manifesto (e.g. 0.08).
corrected_counts = (
    corrected_df.assign(**{col: corrected_df[col].astype(int) for col in LLM_CATEGORIES})
    .groupby(["year", "manifesto"], as_index=False)[LLM_CATEGORIES]
    .sum()
)
scores_df = summary_df[["year", "label", "sentence_count", "climate_salience_share"]].merge(
    corrected_counts, left_on=["year", "label"], right_on=["year", "manifesto"], how="left"
)
scores_df[LLM_CATEGORIES] = scores_df[LLM_CATEGORIES].fillna(0).div(scores_df["sentence_count"], axis=0)

SCORE_SHEET_COLUMNS = ["climate_salience_share", *LLM_CATEGORIES, "sentence_count"]
scores_by_candidate = add_family_dummies(to_candidate_level(scores_df, "year", "label", SCORE_SHEET_COLUMNS))

# --- Sheet 2: party families (mining stance) only, 1/0 per family ------------------------
families_by_candidate = add_family_dummies(
    scores_by_candidate[["year", "candidate", "party", "manifesto_label"]].copy()
)

candidate_year_output_path = COMPARISON_DIR / "manifesto_scores_families_2022_2026.xlsx"
with pd.ExcelWriter(candidate_year_output_path, engine="openpyxl") as writer:
    scores_by_candidate.to_excel(writer, index=False, sheet_name="scores")
    families_by_candidate.to_excel(writer, index=False, sheet_name="party_families")

print(f"Saved: {candidate_year_output_path}")
print(f"  scores: {len(scores_by_candidate)} candidate-years; party_families: {len(families_by_candidate)} candidate-years")
display(scores_by_candidate)
display(families_by_candidate)

# Stacked bar chart of the validated manifesto scores, one panel per year (2022 left,
# 2026 right). Each bar's total height is the policlim climate-salience score ("all": the
# share of a manifesto's sentences that are climate-relevant). Its segments are the four
# LLM categories from corrected_df, as shares of the same sentence total, so each segment
# is that category's part of the climate-salience score. The remainder - climate-relevant
# sentences assigned to none of the four categories, including those below the 0.8
# climate-score threshold that were never sent to the LLM - is drawn in gray as "Other
# climate-relevant", so the stack always sums to the policlim score.
# Built from scores_by_candidate (export cell above): validated data, Claudia López excluded.
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.ticker import PercentFormatter

# Colors: softened tints of categorical slots 1-4 of the reference palette, in their fixed
# order. Validated as a set (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD separation): the yellow is
# kept at its documented step because any lighter yellow leaves the lightness band. The
# residual is a remainder, not an identity, so it takes a light neutral gray. All text
# uses the ink tokens, never a series color.
SEGMENTS = [
    ("pro_just_transition", "Pro-just transition",    "#6da7ec"),
    ("anti_ff",             "Anti fossil fuel",       "#f2956f"),
    ("pro_ff",              "Pro fossil fuel",        "#5cc8a2"),
    ("energy_security",     "Energy security",        "#eda100"),
    ("other_climate",       "Other climate-relevant", "#d9d8d1"),
]
SURFACE, INK, INK_SECONDARY, INK_MUTED = "#fcfcfb", "#0b0b0b", "#52514e", "#898781"
GRID, BASELINE = "#e1e0d9", "#c3c2b7"

SHORT_NAMES = {
    "Federico Gutiérrez": "Gutiérrez", "Gustavo Petro": "Petro", "Rodolfo Hernández": "Hernández",
    "Sergio Fajardo": "Fajardo", "Abelardo De La Espriella": "De la Espriella",
    "Iván Cepeda Castro": "Cepeda", "Paloma Valencia Laserna": "Valencia",
}

plot_df = scores_by_candidate[["year", "candidate", "party", "climate_salience_share", *LLM_CATEGORIES]].copy()
plot_df["other_climate"] = plot_df["climate_salience_share"] - plot_df[LLM_CATEGORIES].sum(axis=1)
overshoot = plot_df["other_climate"] < -1e-9
if overshoot.any():
    # Multi-label sentences can push the four categories above the salience share; the
    # stack would then overstate the total, so say so instead of clipping silently.
    print("Warning: LLM category shares exceed climate salience for:",
          plot_df.loc[overshoot, ["year", "candidate"]].to_dict("records"))
plot_df["other_climate"] = plot_df["other_climate"].clip(lower=0)

years = sorted(plot_df["year"].unique())
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, len(years), figsize=(12, 5.8), sharey=True, facecolor=SURFACE)
bar_width = 0.55
y_max = plot_df["climate_salience_share"].max() * 100 * 1.15

for ax, year in zip(axes, years):
    year_df = plot_df[plot_df["year"] == year].sort_values("climate_salience_share", ascending=False)
    x = list(range(len(year_df)))
    bottoms = pd.Series(0.0, index=year_df.index)
    for column, label, color in SEGMENTS:
        # The surface-colored edge is the 2px gap that separates stacked segments.
        ax.bar(x, year_df[column] * 100, bar_width, bottom=bottoms * 100, color=color,
               label=label, edgecolor=SURFACE, linewidth=1.5)
        bottoms = bottoms + year_df[column]
    # Direct-label only the total (the policlim score) on each cap; the legend and the
    # scores sheet carry the segment values.
    for xi, total in zip(x, year_df["climate_salience_share"] * 100):
        ax.text(xi, total + y_max * 0.015, f"{total:.1f}%", ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9, color=INK)
    ax.set_xticks(x)
    # Candidate surname only; the party is carried by the scores sheet / table view below.
    ax.set_xticklabels([SHORT_NAMES[candidate] for candidate in year_df["candidate"]],
                       fontsize=10, color=INK_SECONDARY)
    ax.set_title(str(year), loc="left", fontsize=12, color=INK, pad=8)
    ax.set_facecolor(SURFACE)
    ax.set_ylim(0, y_max)
    ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(PercentFormatter(decimals=0))
    ax.grid(axis="y", color=GRID, linewidth=1, linestyle="-")
    ax.set_axisbelow(True)
    ax.tick_params(axis="y", colors=INK_MUTED, length=0, labelsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(axis="x", length=0)
    for spine in ("top", "right", "left"):
        ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
    ax.spines["bottom"].set_color(BASELINE)

axes[0].set_ylabel("Share of all manifesto sentences", color=INK_SECONDARY, fontsize=10)
handles, labels = axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels()
fig.legend(handles, labels, loc="lower center", ncol=len(SEGMENTS), frameon=False, fontsize=9,
           bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 0.0), labelcolor=INK_SECONDARY, handlelength=1.2, columnspacing=1.6)
fig.suptitle("",
             x=0.02, y=0.995, ha="left", fontsize=13, color=INK)
fig.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0.07, 1, 0.97])

stacked_scores_path = COMPARISON_DIR / "manifesto_scores_stacked_by_year.png"
fig.savefig(stacked_scores_path, dpi=200, bbox_inches="tight", facecolor=SURFACE)
plt.show()
print(f"Saved: {stacked_scores_path}")

# Table view of exactly what is drawn (percent of all manifesto sentences).
display(
    plot_df.assign(**{col: (plot_df[col] * 100).round(1) for col, _, _ in SEGMENTS})
    .assign(climate_salience_share=(plot_df["climate_salience_share"] * 100).round(1))
    .rename(columns={"climate_salience_share": "all (policlim)", **{col: label for col, label, _ in SEGMENTS}})
)
